clue.text: One-time citizen's infant boy consuming half of capital

indicators.note: the baby and the boy eat up, so hold inside, the next part

parts.note: an infant is a baby
Ian is a boy's name

indicators.note: the first half of the word's six letters is taken

parts.note: London is the UK capital

explanation.surface: A former resident's little son is said to have eaten up half a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' puts LON, half of LONDON, between BABY and IAN; the 's after 'citizen' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Babylonian lived in ancient Babylon, a city long gone, so is a citizen of the past.

clue.text: Most appropriate accommodation for a farm animal

indicators.note: the word for most appropriate provides room for the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: best means most suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: The best housing for a creature on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation for' puts A inside BEST; 'accommodation' looks like a stable but is a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beast is an old word for a farm animal, as in beasts of the field or cattle.

clue.text: I share in light meal comprising two elements

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the light meal word

parts.note: a bite is a quick snack
a part is a share

explanation.surface: Splitting a snack into two halves to share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and PART inside BITE, after the BI.
explanation.definitionFit: Bipartite means having two parts, as in a bipartite agreement between two sides.

clue.text: Bishops left US airports I'd left, surprisingly

indicators.note: in an unexpected way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L again, the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Some clergy have flown out of American airports, which is surprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges US, AIRPORTS and I'D, and each 'left' gives an L, one at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lords Spiritual are the Church of England bishops who sit in the House of Lords, Britain's upper chamber.

clue.text: Sister's position: not one picked up by poet

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: none means not one
Thomas Hood was an English poet

explanation.surface: A nun's status: none of her verses was noticed by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' gives NUN from the sound of NONE; HOOD is the 19th-century poet Thomas Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Nunhood is the state of being a nun, the role a religious sister holds.

clue.text: Article by this writer's not so lacking in purpose

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
this writer is I, the setter; this writer's = I'm, I am
less means not so much

explanation.surface: A writer's article is no better, and pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer's' reads as I'm (I am); 'by' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless means without aim or direction, having no goal or purpose.

clue.text: Where a cobbler may be, missing Times unfortunately

indicators.note: missing means going without, so the letters named next are dropped

parts.note: a cobbler works at his last, the foot-shaped block for shoes
T is the abbreviation for time; plural Times gives two Ts

explanation.surface: A shoemaker is absent from the newspaper, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes both Ts out of AT LAST. 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is two time abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, used where one might say sadly or unfortunately.

clue.text: Plant a great number around university

indicators.note: the word for a great number goes around the letter

parts.note: lots means a great number

explanation.surface: Many plants grow around a university campus.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water plant, the sacred lily of Asia.

clue.text: Darkish-coloured pan Lady Jane possibly used?

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, as is to slate
Lady Jane Grey was the nine-days queen of England; possibly marks her surname as one example of Grey

explanation.surface: A dark cooking pan that Lady Jane might have used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pan' looks like a cooking pot but is the verb to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: Slate-grey is a dull bluish-grey, the shade of roofing slate, so a darkish colour.

clue.text: Slovenly nature of old nurse drinking coffee at bar on ship

indicators.note: the nurse takes the coffee in, so it goes inside

parts.note: SRN is State Registered Nurse, a former British nursing title
a latte is a milky coffee
a bar is a line, as on a chart
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A retired nurse is untidy, drinking coffee at a bar aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' puts LATTE inside SRN, then LINE and SS follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Slatternliness is being slatternly: dirty and untidy in habits or appearance.

clue.text: Endless longing for painkiller

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: aspiring is longing or yearning for something

explanation.surface: Endless craving for a painkiller, as an addict might feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts the G off ASPIRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common analgesic drug taken to relieve headaches and other pain.

clue.text: Reserve force with revolutionary goal, keeping one illuminated

indicators.note: the reversed goal holds the following pieces within it
turning round as in a revolution, so the word for goal is read backwards

parts.note: an aim is a goal
I is the Roman numeral one
lit means illuminated

explanation.surface: A rebel army with a revolutionary aim, lit up by its cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns AIM into MIA, and 'keeping' puts I and LIT inside it after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a body of civilian soldiers held in reserve for emergencies, not a regular army.

clue.text: Wading bird changes colour

parts.note: to turn is to change, as milk turns
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A wading bird changes colour with the seasons.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnstone is a shorebird that flips over stones on beaches looking for food.

clue.text: Discernment of staff originally employed in gallery

indicators.note: put to work inside, so the letter goes into the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter is used

explanation.surface: The good judgement of people first hired to work at an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives S from 'staff', and 'employed in' places it inside TATE, the London gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is the ability to judge what is good or fitting, especially in art and style.

clue.text: Economise, writing novel in health resort, mostly

indicators.note: the novel's title sits inside the shortened resort
most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
Kim is the novel by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: Cutting costs by writing a novel while staying at a spa, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims SPA to SP, and KIM, Kipling's novel, goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to spend or use as little as possible, cutting corners to save money.

clue.text: Rascal caught in narrow channel on lake

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the channel word

parts.note: a sound is a narrow sea channel
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
re means on or concerning
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A villain is captured in a narrow strait by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside SOUND; RE means 'on' as in regarding.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest rogue, a rascal or villain.

clue.text: Remove arms from girl's political representative?

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so girl's is Di's
a member, as in Member of Parliament, represents voters

explanation.surface: Taking away the guns from a young woman's MP, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'remove arms' as disarming, but the definition means cutting off limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismember is to cut off a body's limbs, so literally to remove its arms.

clue.text: Helmeted woman's time in Bahrain, travelling without husband

indicators.note: moving about, so the letters are rearranged
without means lacking, so the husband's letter is taken away

explanation.surface: A woman's spell in Bahrain, travelling without her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes H from BAHRAIN; 'travelling' rearranges T, IN and BARAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia, the figure personifying Britain, is shown wearing a helmet and holding a trident.

clue.text: Go too far past stretch of river

parts.note: over means past or finished
a reach is a straight stretch of river

explanation.surface: Travelling beyond one stretch of a river and going too far.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreach is to try to do more than one can, exceeding sensible limits.

clue.text: African native given a set of books to carry

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
to bear is to carry

explanation.surface: A local in Africa is given a set of books to lug around.
explanation.definitionFit: The antbear, or aardvark, is a burrowing mammal found only in Africa.

clue.text: Possess way to gather first of ripe crop

indicators.note: the outer words gather the letter in, holding it inside

parts.note: to have is to possess

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word

parts.note: ST is street, a way

explanation.surface: Own a route by which to bring in the ripe crops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' gives R from 'ripe', and 'to gather' puts it inside HAVE, before ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest is the crop gathered in a season, the yield of a field.

clue.text: Curious about current emitting loud sound

indicators.note: around, so the curious word goes about the current symbol

parts.note: nosy means curious or prying
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at an electric current making a loud buzz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps NOSY around I, the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noisy makes a lot of loud sound, like a crowd or engine.

clue.text: Dark period man on board reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the chess piece's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece, a man on the chessboard

explanation.surface: A sinister spell reported by a man aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a sailor, but the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time of darkness between sunset and sunrise.

clue.text: Continental character setting up a male publication

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a publication

explanation.surface: A European figure starts a magazine for men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up' reads A, M and MAG from the bottom upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character from mainland Europe.

clue.text: Period in Alabama principally surveying transport hubs

parts.note: a term is a period of time, as a school term
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

indicators.note: chiefly, so the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A spell in Alabama mainly spent inspecting bus and rail stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminals are the end stations of transport lines, such as airports or bus stations.

clue.text: Latin American dance additionally used briefly in South Africa

indicators.note: the shortened word sits inside the country's letters
cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: also means additionally

explanation.surface: A Latin dance is also briefly taken up in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims ALSO to ALS, which goes 'in' SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively dance of Latin American origin, set to Cuban-style music.

clue.text: Current measure blocking fashion for disorderly behaviour

indicators.note: the unit blocks or sits in the middle of the fashion word

parts.note: the rage is the current fashion, as in all the rage
an amp measures electric current

explanation.surface: A unit of electricity stops a fashion craze becoming a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' puts AMP inside RAGE; 'Current' looks like up-to-date but means electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a spell of violent, uncontrolled behaviour, like a mob running riot.

clue.text: Head off duck trapping seabird — it's never-ending!

indicators.note: the shortened duck catches the seabird inside
the head, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: a teal is a small duck
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A headless duck catches a seabird, and the story goes on for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' cuts TEAL to EAL, and 'trapping' holds TERN inside it after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting for ever, without beginning or end.

clue.text: Solitary-sounding advance

indicators.note: sounding like the word for solitary, so it is said aloud

parts.note: lone means solitary, alone

explanation.surface: A lonely-sounding step forward.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance is money lent ahead of time, a loan.

clue.text: European capital initially involved in urchin's discharge

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the urchin's word

parts.note: a brat is an urchin, so urchin's gives BRAT'S

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word

parts.note: lava is what a volcano discharges

explanation.surface: A capital city starts to be caught up in a street child's outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives I from 'involved', which goes 'in' BRATS, before LAVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Bratislava is the capital city of Slovakia, on the Danube.
